Dr. Satya Prakash Dash, CEO, IKP Knowledge Park, joined the valedictory ceremony of ICRISAT’s ISSCA–ITEC international training programme on “𝗠𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗧𝗲𝗰𝗵𝗻𝗼𝗹𝗼𝗴𝘆 𝗧𝗿𝗮𝗻𝘀𝗳𝗲𝗿: 𝗔 𝗚𝗹𝗼𝗯𝗮𝗹 𝗣𝗮𝘁𝗵𝘄𝗮𝘆 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗗𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗹𝗼𝗽𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗖𝗼𝘂𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗲𝘀.”

Held at ICRISAT, the programme converged 44 mid-to-senior professionals from 20 countries across the Global South for a two-week learning experience focused on technology transfer, including the application of AI in research, scientific communication, and data analysis.

As Chief Guest, Dr. Dash shared remarks on the importance of collaboration among the Global South countries and joined the ICRISAT leadership team in presenting certificates to the participants, marking the culmination of their learning journey.

Earlier in the programme, our colleague Dr. Vithal K Lakkineni, Ph.D. engaged with the participants and shared practical perspectives on “𝗕𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗕𝗿𝗶𝗱𝗴𝗲𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗜𝗻𝗻𝗼𝘃𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻: 𝗣𝗮𝗿𝘁𝗻𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗽𝘀, 𝗙𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗚𝗹𝗼𝗯𝗮𝗹 𝗦𝗼𝘂𝘁𝗵 𝗖𝗼𝗹𝗹𝗮𝗯𝗼𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻,” highlighting the importance of partnerships and collaborative approaches in advancing innovation across emerging ecosystems.

We are pleased to support platforms that foster global knowledge exchange, technology transfer, and innovation capacity-building across the Global South.

We congratulate ICRISAT and all the participants on the successful completion of the programme and wish them continued success as they apply their learnings to advance innovation and technology transfer in their respective countries.

Building evidence-driven healthcare innovation for India

Society for Innovation & Entrepreneurship - SINE IIT Bombay hosted an HTA Workshop on 7 August 2026, in collaboration with DHR, HTAIn, and ICMR–NIRRWoH, bringing together ~100 startups, innovators, researchers, and healthcare stakeholders online and in person.

The workshop covered HTA fundamentals, evidence and data requirements, study parameters, and decision-making, with practical case studies helping startups apply these concepts to their technologies.

The session highlighted the importance of integrating HTA and evidence generation early to help startups navigate the path from technology development to healthcare adoption and impact.

A special thanks to Dr. Shankar Prinja for his insightful session on “AI in Healthcare Technology Assessment: Opportunities and Challenges.”

We sincerely thank Dr. Beena Joshi, Dr. Oshima Sachin, Dr. Yogesh Gurav, Dr. Manju Sengar and her team, along with all the speakers - Dr. Sivasubramaniam S A, Dr.varun kashyap, Dr. Asim, and Ms. Tejal R Varekar for sharing their valuable insights and making the workshop a meaningful learning experience. 

We also thank all the participants for their enthusiastic participation and valuable contributions. 

A special thanks to Dr. Balu Venugopal for initiating this important engagement.

We look forward to continued engagement through follow-up sessions and startup-specific HTA interactions, helping innovators build evidence-driven technologies ready for assessment and adoption.

Day 3 | Partnerships, Fundraising Readiness & Founder Evolution

The final day of DERBI Foundation’s Acceleration Program focused on building long-term scale engines - partnerships, investor readiness, and leadership evolution.

We began with “Channel & Partnerships: Designing a Partner Engine That Scales,” led by Venkat Shyam. Founders explored how structured channel #strategies, aligned incentives, and ecosystem #collaborations can unlock non-linear growth beyond direct sales.

In the #Fundraising Deep Dive: #Investor-Grade Company — From Pitch to Process & Metrics That Raise Money, Ravindra Krishnappa emphasized building companies that are investment-ready by design. The session broke down traction KPIs, investors' trust, #governance discipline, narrative clarity, and process maturity.

The program concluded with “Org & Leadership for Scaling: Founder-to-CEO Transition” led by Sathyanarayana B V, followed by final reflections and key takeaways. The conversation centered on building leadership depth, creating accountable org structures, and evolving from operator to strategic decision-maker. Sathyanarayana B V also spoke about #HR Management Grid, Leadership styles, how each one of them affects and has an impact in different workplaces, and how leaders are born or lost under different #leadership style

Scaling a startup ultimately requires more than #strategy - it demands founder transformation.

We thank all our expert #mentors and participating #founders for making this acceleration journey deeply insightful and impact-driven. At DERBI Foundation, our commitment remains clear: enabling startups with the right #ecosystem, right #frameworks, and right #mentorship to scale sustainably.

Day 2 | Expanding Markets, Strengthening Financial Foundations

Day 2 of DERBI Foundation’s Acceleration Program shifted the lens from internal readiness to external expansion and financial resilience.

The day opened with “Market Access Strategy: #IndiaExpansion + Global Entry Readiness” led by Shivi Jain. Startups explored structured approaches to entering new markets, from regulatory preparedness and localization strategy to channel partnerships and #global positioning. The focus was on building scalable access, not opportunistic expansion.

In the Cashflow & Working Capital War-Room: Scale Without Dying, Nayak guided founders through one of the most underestimated growth levers — liquidity discipline. Through real-world scenarios and financial stress-testing frameworks, startups examined burn cycles, receivables management, and #capital efficiency as core survival metrics.

The day concluded with “Deal Structuring & Term Sheet Masterclass: Don’t Lose the Company” by Sharath Shyamasunder, The Startup Zone, where founders unpacked #investor clauses, dilution mechanics, control rights, and long-term implications of #fundraising decisions.

Growth is exciting. But #sustainable scale is built on informed expansion, disciplined capital management, and smart deal-making.

Two of the ten innovations recognised in the H&M Foundation's Global Change Award 2026 are companies we have backed at Social Alpha.

https://lnkd.in/gAtXh9jX

CanvaLoop, whose Agro-Lyocell turns agricultural residue into regenerated cellulosic fibre — a forest-free alternative to the wood that conventional viscose still consumes.

Microbeworks Scientific, whose MicroBlue produces biodegradable dyes through microbial fermentation, is engineered to run on the dyeing infrastructure the industry already owns rather than demanding it be rebuilt.

Fashion's footprint will not be fixed by pledges, capsule collections, or the word "sustainable" stretched until it means nothing. It will be fixed by people willing to carry hard science out of the laboratory and onto the factory floor — and to absorb the translational risk that journey demands.

That is the work. It is slow, unglamorous, and rarely rewarded by the narrative economy. A prize like this matters because, for once, it points the spotlight at the right thing.

Congratulations to both teams. The recognition is earned. The harder part — deployment at scale — is what we get to do next, together.

Work In Progress – August 2026 edition is here.
 
Last month, Social Alpha became a Stanford Graduate School of Business case study, one that examines a decade-long attempt to prove that markets for early-stage deep tech innovation aren't found. They're built, deliberately, by de-risking the innovation till it finds its way to the people it was meant to serve.
 
It's a fitting frame for an edition that's really about the same question: what does it take for an idea to outgrow the lab and take root in the world? From conversations on inclusive finance to national and global recognitions, from new government partnerships to fresh funding rounds, this edition tracks that slow, unglamorous work of adoption, the part that rarely makes headlines but is where innovation actually earns its keep.

"If we are growing, we actually have a problem."

That is Manoj Kumar, founder of Social Alpha, on his measure of success: an institution built to make itself unnecessary.

Over ten years, Social Alpha has backed more than 450 Indian start-ups solving problems conventional capital would not touch: a cryogen-free MRI machine, biodigesters running in more than 100,000 households, incense sticks made from temple flowers pulled from the Ganges. Those companies have gone on to raise more than $150 million in follow-on capital.

Social Alpha's wager is that markets can be built. De-risk the venture, align state, society, and capital, and a risk mainstream investors once refused becomes one they can underwrite.

I spent the past several months writing the Stanford University Graduate School of Business GSB case on Social Alpha with Professor William Barnett. What Manoj, Vidya Phalke, and the full team at Social Alpha have built deserves to be studied, and replicated well beyond India.
